spec_features.spec_quote: Maximum turns (default 20), agents stop at limit or explicit give-up
spec_features.evidence: config.py:24 MAX_TURNS = 20; agent_runner.py:120 `for turn_num in range(1, max_turns + 1):` bounds the agent loop so iteration stops at the limit; main.py:108 passes max_turns into AgentRunner.run. The cap actually bounds execution.
spec_features.notes: The 'explicit give-up' part is handled by a separate mechanism (_should_terminate). The turn cap itself is genuinely enforced as the loop's upper bound.

spec_features.spec_quote: Default to 20 turns (enough for degradation to emerge) but configurable
spec_features.evidence: config.py:24 MAX_TURNS = 20 (default); main.py:210-216 argparse `--max-turns` default=MAX_TURNS, threaded through run_evaluation -> AgentRunner.run (agent_runner.py:73 max_turns param) which bounds the loop at agent_runner.py:120. Both the default value and configurability are real.
spec_features.notes: Same enforced loop bound as above; this entry covers the default+configurable aspect, which is implemented.

spec_features.spec_quote: agents stop at limit or explicit give-up
spec_features.evidence: agent_runner.py:132 `if self._should_terminate(transcript): break` actually breaks the loop. _should_terminate (agent_runner.py:235-259) scans the agent's last statement for give_up_indicators ('cannot solve','impossible','i give up','quit','stop trying','exit','abort','cannot be solved') and returns True, stopping the run. Mechanism is wired and honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Detection is keyword-based and brittle (e.g. mock_agent's give-up statement says 'unsolvable', which is not in the list, so it would NOT trigger). But for matching distress/give-up phrases the loop does break, so enforcement is real.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Check if the agent should be stopped (gave up, too frustrated, etc)

spec_features.spec_quote: Can limit attempts per turn (prevents token exhaustion)
spec_features.evidence: No per-turn attempt cap exists. agent_runner.py:180 `for tool_spec in tool_calls_spec:` executes ALL tool calls the agent requests with no count limit. MAX_EDITS = 50 (config.py:162) is the closest config but it is never imported or read anywhere (grep shows only the definition). max_legitimate_attempts (config.py:44/52/59/66) is a dataclass field never read at runtime by mock_agent/judge/analysis/runner. So nothing limits attempts per turn.
spec_features.notes: Pure DESIGN.md prose ('Can limit attempts per turn' DESIGN.md:318). MAX_EDITS is an unused constant; max_legitimate_attempts is an unread dataclass attribute.
